sources.title: NGSS MS-ESS3-5: Ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century
Earle, Physical Geology 2nd ed. (BCcampus), 19.1 What Makes the Climate Change?
Earle, Physical Geology 2nd ed. (BCcampus), 19.2 Anthropogenic Climate Change

note.text: Sunlight warms Earth. The air above controls how much of that heat escapes back to space.

steps.title: Atmosphere
steps.instruction: Trace the top of the atmosphere.

note.text: The atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, which don't trap heat.
Energy reaches Earth from the sun as light.

steps.title: Sunlight
steps.instruction: Draw sunlight passing through the air to the ground.

note.text: Sunlight passes through the air and warms the ground.

steps.title: Heat rising
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of heat leaving the ground.

note.text: The warm ground gives off invisible infrared radiation: heat energy.

steps.title: Escaping
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of heat escaping to space.

note.text: Some of that heat escapes out to space.

steps.title: Sent back
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of heat sent back down.

note.text: Greenhouse gases absorb some heat and send it out in all directions, some back down. This warms the surface.

steps.title: Greenhouse gas
steps.instruction: Trace the two carbon dioxide molecules.

note.text: Gases with three or more atoms, like carbon dioxide (CO2), methane and water vapor, are greenhouse gases.
Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon that was stored underground for millions of years, as CO2.

steps.title: Emissions
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of CO2 rising.

note.text: Earth is now about 1 °C warmer than before industry, and two-thirds of that warming came after 1975.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: How does adding more carbon dioxide to the air raise Earth's temperature?

options.text: More of the ground's heat is absorbed and sent back down instead of escaping
options.feedback: Yes. More greenhouse gas means less heat escapes to space, so the surface warms.

options.text: Carbon dioxide makes the sun shine brighter
options.feedback: CO2 doesn't change the sun. It traps heat leaving the ground.
The gas itself isn't the heat source. It traps heat that would escape.
Sunlight still gets through. CO2 traps the heat the ground gives off.

steps.title: Ask a good question
steps.question: Someone says the warming of the past century was caused by the sun. Which question would best test that?

options.text: Has the sun's energy output actually increased over the past century?
options.feedback: Right. A good question asks for evidence. Scientists compare the sun's measured output with the temperature record.
Everyone agrees the sun is hot. The question is whether its output changed.
That's opinion, not evidence about the cause of warming.
Its distance barely changes. Ask whether its energy output has gone up.
